classification.difficultyReason: Match vertices using supplied angle values or markers, then transfer that correspondence to sides, angle names and ordered similarity statements. The tables scaffold this direct application, including for differently oriented triangles.

content.prompt: Identify the corresponding sides and write a similarity statement.

spec.description: Unfilled, similarly oriented right triangles with all printed labels and angle givens. Coordinates establish appearance only and are not additional measurements.
spec.mathematics: A corresponds to R, B to P and C to Q. Right angles occur at A and R; angles C and Q are 40 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertex labels, right-angle marks and 40-degree givens are visible.

answer.worked:
The right angles match $A$ with $R$, and the $40^\circ$ angles match $C$ with $Q$, so $B$ matches $P$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=\angle RPQ\\\angle BCA&=\angle PQR\end{aligned}$$
Corresponding sides are $BC$ and $PQ$, $AC$ and $RQ$, and $AB$ and $RP$.
$$ABC\sim RPQ$$

spec.description: Two unfilled similar pentagons with clipped upper-left corners, larger above smaller. No numerical dimensions are asserted.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding vertices are A/L, B/M, C/N, D/P and E/Q.

answer.short: $CD\sim NP$, $AE\sim LQ$; $\angle BCD=\angle MNP$, $\angle CDE=\angle NPQ$, $\angle AED=\angle LQP$, $\angle EAB=\angle QLM$; $ABCDE\sim LMNPQ$.
answer.worked:
The corresponding vertices are $A\leftrightarrow L$, $B\leftrightarrow M$, $C\leftrightarrow N$, $D\leftrightarrow P$ and $E\leftrightarrow Q$.
Corresponding sides: $AB\sim LM$, $BC\sim MN$, $CD\sim NP$, $ED\sim QP$, $AE\sim LQ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=\angle LMN\\\angle BCD&=\angle MNP\\\angle CDE&=\angle NPQ\\\angle AED&=\angle LQP\\\angle EAB&=\angle QLM\end{aligned}$$
$$ABCDE\sim LMNPQ$$

spec.description: Unfilled inverted DEF and upright JKL; coordinates derive triangles with the printed 80, 60 and 40 degree angles. All six numerical angle labels and arcs remain.
spec.mathematics: D/L are 80 degrees, E/K are 60 degrees and F/J are 40 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: All vertex and angle givens remain visible; no response answers are drawn.

answer.short: $DE\sim LK$, $EF\sim KJ$, $FD\sim JL$; $\angle EFD=\angle KJL$, $\angle FDE=\angle JLK$; $DEF\sim LKJ$.
answer.worked:
Match the equal angles: $D\leftrightarrow L$ ($80^\circ$), $E\leftrightarrow K$ ($60^\circ$), $F\leftrightarrow J$ ($40^\circ$).
Corresponding sides: $DE\sim LK$, $EF\sim KJ$, $FD\sim JL$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle DEF&=\angle LKJ\\\angle EFD&=\angle KJL\\\angle FDE&=\angle JLK\end{aligned}$$
$$DEF\sim LKJ$$

spec.description: Unfilled similar triangles in the source orientations. Matching single arcs at N/T and double arcs at P/U determine correspondence; no numerical angles or lengths are introduced.
spec.mathematics: M corresponds to V, N to T and P to U.
spec.answerVisibility: Only vertex labels and supplied matching angle arcs are visible.

answer.short: $MP\sim VU$, $PN\sim UT$, $NM\sim TV$; $\angle MPN=\angle VUT$, $\angle PNM=\angle UTV$, $\angle NMP=\angle TVU$; $MPN\sim VUT$.
answer.worked:
The double arcs match $P$ with $U$, and the single arcs match $N$ with $T$, so $M$ matches $V$.
Corresponding sides: $MP\sim VU$, $PN\sim UT$, $NM\sim TV$.
$$\begin{aligned}\angle MPN&=\angle VUT\\\angle PNM&=\angle UTV\\\angle NMP&=\angle TVU\end{aligned}$$
$$MPN\sim VUT$$
